newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Samurai to boost June S.African reserves.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Samurai to boost June S.African reserves.

text.p: South African reserves are expected to be bolstered further in June from record levels in May by the government's 40 billion yen samurai bond issue at the beginning of June.
The bond, with a pay date of June 17, will contribute 1.54 billion rand to the central bank's June reserves.

Economists estimate that the proceeds, lumped together with healthy portfolio investment flows, will help the central bank's gold and foreign exchange reserves climb nearly three billion rand to 24.68 billion from May's 21.80 billion.
This represents around two and a half months import cover, sharply up from around 1.2 months of import cover at the start of the year, economists noted.
Forecasts by the ten economists polled ranged between 23 billion rand to 28 billion rand.
The headline reserves figure for the month will be released at 1600 GMT on July 1 -- the same day South African individuals will be allowed to invest offshore for the first time.
Economists said the continuing build up in reserves would further reassure the markets that the Reserve Bank would be able to smooth market volatilitity in the event of a large outflow of capital.

"We've got enough in the kitty to manage the process of exchange control relaxation and we'll probably see reserves significantly higher at the end of the year," SMK Securities economist Herman van Papendorp said.
"All in all it's a pretty rosy picture as far as interest rates in the next few months are concerned," he added.

Capital inflows were probably higher than those reflected in the sharp decline in the money market shortage by almost 1.5 billion rand during the month due to the Reserve Bank mopping up liquidity in the market, he noted.
Around 3.8 billion rand in foreign purchases of shares and bonds are expected to have contributed to building up reserves in the month.
BOE Natwest economist Nick Barnardt said the government bond issues would to some extent be offset by seasonal outflows of dividend and interest payments at the June half-year end.
He also expected good foreign purchases of shares specifically to be neutralised by the seasonal outflows.
"It depends a lot on the trade. If the trade balance is as good again in June as in May of course then the reserves could be up more," he said.
In May, the trade balance jumped to another surplus of 1.746 billion rand from a 725 million rand surplus the month before, due mainly to a sharp slowdown in imports.
Government's successful 20 year $500 million Yankee bond issue -- announced in the middle of June -- was seen flowing into the July reserves figure.

Lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co Inc announced that the issue came in at a 183 basis point spread above similar dated U.S. Treasuries compared to the country's first Yankee issue which came in at a 195-point spread over 10 years.
Around 2.4 billion rand from the dollar bond is expected to enter the reserves in July after the 1.5 billion rand from the 40 billion yen samurai in June.
